title: You are taller in the morning
hook: Most people are about a centimetre taller when they wake than at bedtime.
peek: People are usually around a centimetre taller first thing in the morning. The discs that cushion the spine settle a little during the day and recover overnight. In space, astronauts grow taller still.
lede: Measure yourself first thing in the morning and again before bed, and the numbers will probably differ by about a centimetre. The cause is the spine. Between its bones sit soft, springy discs that work like cushions. All day, standing and walking press them a little flatter. Lying down at night takes the load off, and they plump back up.

bullets.text: There are 23 of these discs along the spine. Each one loses only a sliver of height in a day, but together they add up to the difference between your morning and evening height.
Because height changes through the day, careful studies of growth try to measure people at a consistent time. Otherwise a morning reading and an evening reading can look like growth or shrinkage.
Without gravity pressing down, the discs expand further. NASA says astronauts can grow up to about 3 percent taller in space, and suits and seats are designed with room for it.

After nearly a year on the International Space Station, astronaut Scott Kelly came home about 5 centimetres taller than his identical twin, Mark. Within days back on Earth he had settled to his usual height.
